scope: Small paired pilot of assistance for the SECOND bite, not M5 acceptance, M6 view following, a multi-seed result, or evidence of clinical benefit. No tuning or replacement trials after scoring.
acquisition: Eight independent full simulations, same verified scene, v1.10 marked nominal seed 0, optics and all two_bite_v1 safety checks. Common setup, exposure, first bite and first direct slit reacquisition. At this checkpoint require identical tissue-node, cutter pose, camera and perception prefix hashes across all eight runs. Apply the registered disturbance on the very next observation. All changes restricted to the second bite and its required withdrawal.
view: One physical nonrespondable foreground occluder: existing occlude_until_camera near-sphere injection. The sphere stays at its world position; changing only the camera can alter its projection. Event injection alone may use scoring geometry. Record actual visibility, refusals and moves; do not assume a changed camera recovered the view.
creep: One registered relax_m (0.5 mm toward the cut line per held arm) using the existing harness; no occluder.
policies: Fixed camera holds its pose at a requested recovery observation slot (25 settling steps), active camera uses the unchanged guarded ECM recovery table, not continuous tracking. Fixed traction retains both grasps without further correction (10 settling steps per held arm per correction slot). Adaptive traction only during a requested tension recovery: compare current RGB-D sheet width with its measured width at first reacquisition. Request half their signed difference per arm, capped at +/-0.2 mm. Reject missing, invalid or sign-conflicting width evidence; the existing model-strain safety band can veto, never set the magnitude or waive a guard. This is a model benchmark, not measured force. All variants retain identical attempt budgets and the two-bite terminal scorer.
decision: For each disturbance and strategy report outcome, both per-bite growths and reacquisitions, park readback, actual camera moves, accepted post-injection traction commands, observations until second closure, peak/terminal length, tear/fault and failure reason. All eight reports and identical initial checkpoint required; if any run exceeds 10 mm, tears or faults, flag that result as unsafe. A fail-closed run counts as a task failure. Report the paired table even with no improvement. Do not interpret a one-seed contrast as statistical superiority.
